messages:
incident-bot: PAGER ALERT — p95 latency spike for /v1/generate in eu-west-1 during release wave. Metrics: p95 ~1.2s (baseline 120ms), error rate up 0.3%. Canary group shows kernel fallback to CPU. Trigger: latency_slo_breach. Paging @alice_oncall :rotating_light:

alice_oncall: ack. I'm watching graphs now, pulling canary logs.

alice_oncall: can someone paste release id and git sha for the mid-wave?

maria_prod: release midwave-2026-03-17-2, sha=abcdef12 (deployed to canary eu-west-1 5m ago).

diego: seeing large prefetch queue and KV-cache miss spike on nodes handling canary. Batching is collapsing to microbatches (batch size 1-2). Host logs show fallback path selected: `kernel_select->cpu_fallback` on several instances.

diego: quick snippet from host-17 logs: ```[17:03:12] kernel_select: preferred_gpu_kernel failed -> falling back cpu; batch_window_ms=2; kv_miss=0.82```

alice_oncall: ugh. That matches the tail latency. Two options: flip prefetch flag (kill-switch) for canary or roll back the canary. Recommend toggling feature flag first to confirm mitigation.

maria_prod: flipping `midwave_prefetch_enabled` OFF for canary group now.

pagerduty-bot: PATCH /flags/midwave_prefetch_enabled -> success (targets: canary eu-west-1).

ops-bot: traffic routing update: shifting 50% of canary traffic to stable pool to reduce pressure.

diego: after flag flip I still see kernel fallback on ~30% of canary hosts but queue depth dropped ~40%. p95 improving from 1.2s -> 480ms.

alice_oncall: good. Continue monitoring for 5m. If p95 < 300ms and stable, we'll keep release, otherwise rollback.

maria_prod: CS report shows 8 enterprise customers in eu-west saw anomalous >1s tail; no spikes in 5xx. Tom from CS standing by to notify.

tom_cs: preparing notice. Will send interim update to impacted customers: "We observed higher-than-normal request latency during today's deployment; mitigation in progress; will follow up with root cause."

diego: kernel fallback logs indicate kernel-selection heuristics changed in the new runtime commit (sha=abcdef12) — likely affinity/selector bug when prefetch is enabled under certain sequence-length distributions.

alice_oncall: we need SRE to check kernel affinity and whether kernel selector rollout should be gated. maria_prod can you open emergency rollback runbook if this degrades again?

maria_prod: opened runbook INC-5467890123-runbook, linking.

incident-bot: NOTE — if we roll back, use rollout-id midwave-2026-03-17-2 -> revert to midwave-2026-03-16-stable.

alice_oncall: 4m since flag flip — p95 now 260ms, error rate back to baseline. My read: kill-switch was effective for canary. Recommend aborting rollout and hold wave. Do not promote.

diego: agree. I'm running a targeted rollback on canary hosts to previous kernel selection config to remove the new heuristic from those hosts (dry run).

ops-bot: rollback command enqueued: `deploy rollback --release midwave-2026-03-17-2 --targets=canary-eu-west-1`

maria_prod: rolling back canary now. Not touching global wave yet.

diego: post-rollback telemetry shows kernel selector reverted and KV miss rate normalized. p95 now ~140ms.

tom_cs: sending customers the update now: mitigation in place, we rolled back canary, monitoring for stability.

alice_oncall: documenting impact: 8 customers affected, transient p95 spike, no data loss/no 5xx. CS owner=tom_cs.

alice_oncall: assigning owners for postmortem: eng-runtime=diego, eng-sre=maria_prod, cs=tom_cs. We'll schedule postmortem in 48h.

alice_oncall: handing incident to diego for next shift and follow-up. Diego, please continue monitoring eu-west and collect kernel selection traces from canary hosts.

diego: on it. I'll also capture perf traces and a reproducible regression test.

alice_oncall: thanks team. Closing pager for now — if tail spikes >500ms again, re-open and escalate to SEV. :thumbsup:
